Whoever follows the truth, and believes in God and what He has revealed to me, then if you wish, then believe, and if you wish, then disbelieve, for if you disbelieve, then your Lord has prepared for you, for your disbelief in Him, a fire whose walls will surround you. But if you believe in Him and act in obedience to Him, then for you is what God has described for the people of His obedience. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve, means: Whoever God wills to have faith - believes, and whoever God wills to disbelieve - disbelieves, and that is his turning away from it. And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills. This is not an absolute statement from God that disbelief is for whomever He wills, and belief is for whomever He wants, because it is a threat and warning. And He made clear that this is the case with His statement, Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire, and the verses after it. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Umar bin Habib, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. He said: It is a threat from God, so it is not beyond my power. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve, and His statement, Do whatever you will, he said: All of this is a threat, not a compromise, nor a bribe, nor a delegation. And His statement, Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire, God Almighty says: Indeed, We have prepared, and it is from the preparation. For the wrongdoers: those who disbelieved in their Lord. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will surround them, he said: for the disbelievers. And his statement, whose walls will surround them, he said: the walls of the Fire that God has prepared for the disbelievers will surround their Lord, and that is, as it was said: a wall of fire surrounds them like the walls of the tent, which is the room that surrounds the tent, as Ru’bah said: Oh, Hakam bin Al-Mundhir bin Al-Jaroud, the canopy of grace is extended over you. As Salama bin Jandal said: He is the one who brought Al-Nu'man a house whose name is Sadur Al-Fuel after the house of Masradaq It means: a house with a canopy. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement, Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will surround them, he said: It is a wall of fire. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of someone who told him, he said: Its canopy will surround them. He said: Smoke will surround the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection, and it is what God said: A shade with three branches. And it has been narrated “from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that regard, a report indicating that the meaning of his saying: “Its canopy will surround them” is that it surrounded them in this world, and that canopy is the sea.” Who said that? Al-Abbas bin Muhammad and Al-Husayn bin Nasr told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umayya, who said: Muhammad bin Hayy bin Ya’la told me, on the authority of Safwan bin Ya’la, on the authority of Ya’la bin Umayya, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sea is Hell. He said: It was said to him: How is that? So he recited this verse, or read this verse: ‘A Fire whose walls will surround them.’ Then he said: By God, I will never enter it - or as long as I live - and not a drop of it will touch me.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ya`mar ibn Bishr told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us: Rashdin ibn Sa`d told us: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The canopies of Hell are four thick walls, each one of which is like a journey of forty years. Bishr told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The canopy of Hell has four walls, the thickness of each one is like a journey of forty years. Bishr told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Amr told me, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Water like molten metal - he said, like cloudy oil - so when he brings it near to him, the scalp of his face falls into it. And His statement, And if they call for help, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, God Almighty says: And if these wrongdoers call for help on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire because of the severity of their thirst, and they seek water, they will be relieved with the water of molten metal. The interpreters differed about the term mahl. Some of them said: It is everything that is melted and dissolved. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Masoud was given a gift of a water-skin made of gold and silver, so he ordered a trench to be dug in the ground, then a large amount of firewood was thrown into it, then that water-skin was thrown into it, until it foamed and dissolved. He said to his servant: Call whoever from the people of Kufa is present with us. So he called a group of people, and when they entered upon him, he said: Do you see this? They said: Yes. He said: We have not seen in the world anything similar to molten metal closer than this gold and silver, when it foams and dissolves. Others said: It is pus and black blood. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And if they call for help, they will be helped with water like molten metal, he said: Pus and blood. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, With water like molten metal, he said: pus and black blood, like the turbidity of oil. Al-Harith said in his hadith: He means his dregs. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, like molten metal, he said: He says: black like the appearance of oil. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, with water like molten brass, that the water of Hell is black, and it is black, and its trees are black, and its people are black. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And if they call for help, they will be helped with water like molten brass, he said: It is thick water like the dregs of oil. Others said: It is something that has reached its peak heat. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja`far and Harun ibn `Antarah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: Al-Mahal is that which has reached its climax. Although the wording of those who said them differed, the meaning of these sayings is similar, because everything that has been melted of lead, gold, or silver has reached its climax, and whatever has been set on fire until it becomes like the dregs of oil has also reached its climax. It was narrated on the authority of Muammar ibn al-Muthanna that he said: I heard al-Muntaj’ ibn Nabhan say: By God, so-and-so is more hateful to me than Ṭā’iyā’ and mahl. We said to him: What are they? He said: Al-Jarba’ and the molasses that slides down from the sides of the bread when it is molten in the fire from the fire, as if it were smooth, red and thin, so it is red. So mahl is any liquid that has been lit until it reaches its peak heat, or it was not liquid, but melted with the fuel on it, and reached the peak of the extreme heat. And His saying, “It burns the faces. What an evil drink!” He, may His praise be glorified, says: That water with which they wash themselves burns their faces. Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me: Haywah ibn Shuraih told us: Baqiyah told us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Busr, this is how Ibn Khalaf said it on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And he will be given to drink of a purulent water, slurping it. He said: It will be brought close to him and he will dislike it, but when it is brought close to him, it will burn his face and the scalp will fall off, and when he drinks it, it will sever his intestines. God says: “And if they call for relief, they will be given relief with water like murky oil, which will burn their faces. What an evil drink!” Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Ibrahim bin Ishaq Al-Talaqani and Omar bin Bishr told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Safwan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Busr, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far and Harun ibn `Antarah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr: Harun said: When the people of Hell are hungry. And Ja`far said: When the people of Hell come, they will cry out to the tree of Zaqqum, and eat from it, and the skin of their faces will peel off. If a passerby were to recognize them, he would recognize the skin of their faces in it. Then thirst will be poured upon them, and they will cry out, and they will be helped with water like molten brass, the heat of which has reached its climax. When they bring it close to their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skin has fallen off, will be roasted by its heat. And His statement, What an evil drink, the Most High says: What an evil drink, this water with which these wrongdoers are relieved in Hell, the description of which is as described in this verse. And His statement, And evil is the resting place, the Most High says: And evil is this Fire which We have prepared for these wrongdoers as a resting place. And the resting place in the speech of the Arabs is the reclining place, and it is said from it: I leaned on it if I reclined, as the poet said: She said to him and she was pleased: Is there not a young man who leads the people to the gazelles of the morning? He meant: And she leaned on her elbow, and the man leaned on his elbow: if he sleeps on his elbow, he does not sleep, and he is leaning on his elbow, as Abu Dhu’ayb al-Hudhali said: The friend slept and I spent the night in comfort as if my eyes had a slaughtered victim in them As for the word comfort, it is said, I have found comfort in you. Mujahid interpreted his statement, And a bad comfort, to mean the community. The novel mentioned that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Murtafiqan means gathered together. Yaqub told me, he said: Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, And an evil resting place. He said: A gathering. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. I do not know of irtifadh in the sense of gathering in the speech of the Arabs, but irtifadh is a verbal noun, either from the word al-marfaq or from al-rafq.
18:30: God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acted in obedience to God, and adhered to His commands and prohibitions - indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did good deeds, so he obeyed God, and followed His commands and prohibitions. Rather, We will reward him for his obedience and his good deeds with Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow. If someone says: Where is the report of the first inna? It is said: It is possible that its report is His saying Indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did good deeds, so the meaning of the statement is: Indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did righteous deeds. So the first statement was left out, and the second was relied upon with the intention of repetition, as it was said They ask you about fighting in the sacred month meaning: about fighting in it, on repetition, and as the poet said: The Caliph, God has clothed him in a royal garment, in which good endings are hoped for. And he narrates: It is permissible that those who believe is a reward, so the meaning of the statement is: Whoever does righteous deeds, then We will not waste his reward, so the fa is implied in his saying we, and it is permissible that its predicate is: Those for them are the Gardens of Eden, so the meaning of the statement is: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, those for them are the Gardens of Eden.
18:31: God the Almighty says: For those who believe and do righteous deeds are gardens of Eden, meaning gardens of residence in the Hereafter. Underneath them rivers flow means rivers flow below them and before them. And God the Almighty said: Underneath them, meaning: below them and before them. They will be adorned therein with bracelets means: They will wear bracelets of gold, and bracelets is the plural of bracelet. And His statement: They will wear green garments of fine silk and silk is the plural of its singular is sandasa, and it is the finest of brocade. And brocade is the thick and coarse of it, and it was said that brocade is silk, and from it is the saying of Al-Muraqqash: You bet they wear feelings once and brocade sometimes as their dress Meaning: And thick brocade. And his saying, reclining therein on couches, he says: reclining in the Gardens of Eden on couches, which are the beds in the chambers, the singular of which is: couch, and from this is the saying of the poet: Cheeks dried up in the walk, as if they were touching the couches with the mourners. And from it is the saying of Al-A’sha: Between the hallway and the side of her curtain and the sofa of the tables And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, on the couches, he said, they are the curtains. Muammar said, and others said: the beds are in the curtains. And His saying, What an excellent reward! He means: What an excellent reward are the Gardens of Eden, and what He, the Most High, described as having been made for those who believed and did righteous deeds. And what an excellent resting place! He means: And what an excellent resting place! These couches in these Gardens which He, the Most High, described as a place to recline in this verse. And He, the Most High, said, And what an excellent resting place! So He feminized the verb in the sense: And what an excellent resting place! If it had been mentioned to make the resting place masculine, it would have been correct. Now, good and bad are only used by the Arabs in speech to indicate praise and blame, not the action. Therefore, they are mentioned in the feminine form, and they are singular with the dual and the plural.
18:32: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And give, O Muhammad, an example for these polytheists who asked you to drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance, such as two men, to one of whom We gave two gardens, meaning We gave him orchards of vineyards, and surrounded them with palm trees, meaning: We surrounded these two orchards with palm trees. And His statement, and placed crops between them, means: We placed crops in the middle of these two orchards.
18:33: And his saying Both gardens produced their fruit means: Both gardens produced their fruit and what was in them of palm trees, vineyards and various types of crops. And he said: Both gardens, then he said: produced, so he made the predicate singular, because both cannot be singular in their singular form, and its original form is kull, and the Arabs sometimes make both singular, and they take it when it is singular to the dual form, some of the rajaz poets said about that: On each of her legs is a single phalanx, both of which are connected by an appendix. He means by both: both, and you do the same with both and both and both if they are added to a definite noun, and the verb comes after them and is made plural and singular. And his saying and you did not wrong anything from it means and you did not decrease anything from the food, rather you gave it completely and completely. And from this is their saying: So-and-so wronged so-and-so his right. If he underestimated it and diminished it, as the poet said: He wronged me, I have no money like this, and he twisted my hand, he twisted his hand, God is the one who prevails over him And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, and you did not wrong anything from it: meaning you did not decrease anything from it. And His saying, And We caused a river to gush forth within them, by the saying of God Almighty: And We caused a river to gush forth within these two gardens, meaning between them and their trees a river. And it was said, And We caused a river to gush forth, so the jim was made heavy in it, because the gushing forth is in the entire river, and that is because the water sways and some of it flows into some of it.
18:34: And his saying, And he had fruit, the reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as, And he had fruit, with a damma on the tha' and the meem. The reciters of that differed as well. Some of them said, He had gold and silver, and they said, That is the fruit, because it is fruitful wealth, meaning abundant. Mention of who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, and he had fruit, he said: gold and silver. And regarding the statement of God Almighty, with his fruit, he said: it is also gold and silver. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, fruit, he said: gold and silver. He said: And his statement, and its fruit is surrounded, is also the same. Others said: Rather, he meant by it: a lot of money from all kinds of money. Who said that? Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ibn Abbas read it as and he had fruit with the dammah, and he said: He means all kinds of money. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And he had fruit, meaning: money. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and he had fruit, he said: of all wealth. Al-Hasan bin Yahya said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and its fruit is surrounded, he said: The fruit of all wealth means the fruit, and other than it is all wealth. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The fruit is all money. He said: And every money that is gathered is fruit if it is of the same color as the fruit and other than it is all money. Others said: Rather, he meant the origin. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And he had fruit, fruit is the root. He said, And his fruit was surrounded, he said: With its root, and it seems that those who directed its meaning to being types of money, meant that it is the plural of fruit, the plural of fruit, just as the book is pluralized as books, and the donkey is a donkey. Some of those who agreed with them in this reading read fruit with a damma on the th and a sukoon on the meem, and he meant the damma in it, but he made it sukoon in order to make it easier. It may be possible that he meant by it the plural of fruit, just as wood is pluralized as wood. Some of the Medinans read that, And he had fruit with a fatha on the th and the meem, as suna is the plural of fruit, just as wood is pluralized as wood, and reed is qasab. The most correct of the reciters in that, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read, Aw kana lahu thamar, with a damma on the th and the meem, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, even though it is the plural of fruit, just as books is the plural of book. The meaning of the words And We caused a river to gush forth within them, and he had from them fruit, meaning from his two gardens, various types of fruit. This has been made clear to those who are guided to understand it, His statement, And We made for one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We surrounded them with palm trees, and We placed between them crops. Then He said: And he had from these vineyards, palm trees, and crops fruit. And His statement, Then he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, God Almighty says: So this one for whom We had given two gardens of grapes said to his companion who had no money while he was addressing him, I have more wealth than you and am stronger in men, meaning: and stronger in clan and tribe, as Uyaynah and Al-Aqra’ said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the leaders of the Arabs and the masters of wealth, so leave us, Salman, Khabbab, and Suhayb, looking down on them and being arrogant towards them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So he said to his companion while he was conversing with him, ‘I have more wealth than you and am stronger in men.’ And by God, that is the desire of the wicked: an abundance of wealth and a strong man.
18:35: God the Most High says: This is the one for whom We made two gardens of grapes. He entered his garden, which is his orchard, while he was unjust to himself. His injustice to himself was his disbelief in the resurrection, his doubt in the occurrence of the Hour, and his forgetting of the return to God the Most High, which caused him to incur God’s wrath and painful punishment. And His statement: He said, ‘I do not think that this will ever perish.’ God the Most High says that when he saw his garden and saw it and what was in it of trees, fruits, crops, and flowing rivers, he doubted the return to God: I do not think that this garden will ever perish, nor will it be destroyed or ruined, and I do not think that the Hour in which God promised His creation the gathering will come and occur.
18:36: Then he made another wish, despite his doubt, and said, And if I am returned to my Lord, and I am returned to Him, and he is not certain that he will return to Him, I will surely find better than it as a return. He says: I will find better than this Paradise of mine with God if I am returned to Him as a return and a destination. He says: He did not give me this Paradise in this world except that I have with Him something better than it in the afterlife if I am returned to Him. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, And I do not think that the Hour will come, he said: He doubted. Then he said: And if that were to happen, then I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a return, He did not give me this except that I have with Him something better than that. Bishr told us, he said: Zaid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself. He said, ‘I do not think that this will ever perish. And I do not think that the Hour will occur.’” Ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord, denying the meeting with Him, and wishing for something from God.
18:37: God Almighty says: He said to the owner of the two gardens, his companion who was less than him in wealth and children, while he was conversing with him: He says: While he was addressing him and speaking to him, Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust? meaning He created your father Adam from dust. Then from a sperm-drop meaning: Then He created you from the sperm-drop of a man and a woman. Then He proportioned you as a man meaning: Then He made you a well-proportioned human being, a man, a male, not a female. He says: Have you disbelieved in He who did this to you, that He would return you as a new creation after you have become dust.
18:38: But He is God my Lord he says: As for me, I do not disbelieve in my Lord, but I am He is God my Lord, meaning that he says: But I say: He is God my Lord and I do not associate anyone with my Lord. There are two ways of reading this: One of them is But He is God my Lord with a shaddah on the noon and deleting the alif in the case of connection, as it is said: I am standing, so the alif is deleted from I, and this is the general reading of the readers of Iraq. As for stopping, the alif is kept in all readings, because the noon is only stressed due to the assimilation of the noon from but, and it is silent in the noon of I, since the hamza in I was dropped, so if one stops on it, the alif in I appears, so it is said: But we, because it is said in stopping on I by confirming the alif, not by dropping it. A group of the people of Hijaz read this: But we by confirming the alif in connection and stopping, and this is even though it is something that is uttered in the necessity of poetry, as the poet said: I am the sword of the tribe, so know me as a praiseworthy man who has scattered the hump So he confirmed the alif in ana, but that is not eloquent speech. The reading that is the correct reading according to us is what we mentioned about the Iraqis, which is deleting the alif from lakin when connected, and confirming it when stopped.
18:39: The Almighty says: Why did you not say, when you entered your garden and were pleased with what you saw of it, Whatever God willed has happened? And there is an omission in the speech that is sufficient to indicate what appeared of it, which is the answer to the condition, and that was. If the speech is directed to this meaning that we have mentioned, then what is in the accusative case because of the occurrence of God’s action upon it, and He willed, and it is permissible to leave out the answer, because the meaning of the speech is known, as it was said: If you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth, and leave the answer, because its meaning is understood. Some of the Arabists used to say that what is in his saying What God willed is in the nominative case with the implication of He, as if it was said: I said He is what God willed. “There is no power except with God,” he says: There is no power to do what we are trying to do in obeying Him except through Him. And his saying If you see, I am less than you in wealth and children, is the saying of the believer who has no wealth or clan, like the owner of the two gardens and his clan, and it is like Salman, Suhaib, and Khabbab, he says: The believer said to the disbeliever: If you see, O man, I am less than you in wealth and children, so if you make I a pillar, you put less in the accusative case, and this is the reading according to us, because it is the reading of the regions, and if you make it a noun, you raise less.
18:40: God Almighty says, informing us about what the believing believer said about the return to God to the disbeliever who doubted the coming of the Hour: If you see, O man, that I am less than you in wealth and children in this world, then perhaps my Lord will provide me with something better than this garden of yours. And send upon it meaning upon the garden of the disbeliever to which he said: I do not think that this will ever perish a punishment from the sky. He says: A torment from the sky that you throw and hurl. Hisbanah is the plural of hisbanah, which means the targets. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He sends upon it a punishment from the sky as a punishment. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: Torment. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And He sends down upon it a punishment from the sky, he said: A punishment. He said: The punishment is a decree from God that He carries out. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The reckoning is the punishment. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, A punishment from the sky, he said: A torment. And His statement, Then it becomes a slippery ground, God Almighty says: Then this garden of yours, O man, becomes a smooth land with nothing in it. Everything in it of plants and vegetation has disappeared, and it has become a desolate, barren wasteland, slippery, with no foot standing on its smooth ground because of its touch, and whatever plants were in it has been obliterated. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then it becomes a slippery ground: meaning that what was in it was harvested and nothing was left in it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Then it becomes a slippery ground, he said: Like a barren land. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then it becomes a slippery ground, he said: A slippery ground and a barren ground are one and the same, in which there is no vegetation.
18:41: And his saying, or its water becomes sunken, means: or its water becomes sunken, so he put sunken, which is a source, in place of sunken, as the poet said: His horses remain saddled with the reins of his saddle Meaning a mourner, and as the other said: Pour out their tears, O hyenas, and answer their wailing, standing up. The Arabs use the word ghor in the plural and dual forms, and use it in the masculine and feminine forms. They say: ghor water, “ghor water,” and ghor waters. By ghor they mean something that has gone and sunk into the ground, so it has gone and the bribe cannot reach it. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Or its water becomes sunken: meaning, it has disappeared and sunk into the ground. And His statement, Then you will not be able to seek it out means: You will not be able to reach the water that was in your garden after it has sunk, by your seeking it.
18:42: God Almighty says: And destruction and calamities surrounded his fruits, which are the various fruits of his garden, to which he used to say: I do not think that these will ever perish. So this unbeliever, the owner of these two gardens, turned his hands upside down, in longing and sorrow. On the loss of his money that he spent in his paradise, while it is empty on its thrones, meaning: while it is empty on its plants and houses. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So he began to turn his hands over: that is, he clapped his hands over what he had spent on it longing for what he had missed, and he said, ‘Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord’ and he said: Oh, I wish I had, he said: This disbeliever wishes after he was afflicted with his Paradise that he had not associated anyone with his Lord, meaning by that: This disbeliever, if he perishes and his worldly life is taken away from him and he is alone with his work, wishes that he had not disbelieved in God or associated anything with Him.
18:43: God Almighty says: The owner of these two gardens did not have a group, and they are the group, as Al-Ajjaj said: Just as the group possesses the quantity In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said, even if some of them differed in their expression of it from our expression, that their meaning is similar to our meaning of it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And he had no group to aid him other than God, he said: His clan. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And he had no company to aid him other than God: meaning, no soldiers to aid him. And His statement, to aid him other than God means: to protect him from God’s punishment and torment if He punishes and torments him. And His statement, And he was not able to defend himself means: and he was not able to protect himself from God’s torment if He tormented him. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And he was not victorious: meaning, he was not immune.
18:44: And His saying, There, the guardianship belongs to God, the Truth. The Almighty says: Then, that is when the torment of the devil befell the owner of the two gardens on the Day of Resurrection. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Wilayat. Some of the people of Medina, Basra, and Kufa read, There is the Wilayat, with a fatha on the waw of the word Wilayat, meaning by that there is allegiance to God, like the statement of God, God is the protector of those who believe, and like His statement, That is because God is the protector of those who believe, referring by it to the guardianship in religion. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it, There is the Wilayat, with a kasra on the waw: from the word king and sultan, from the saying of the speaker: And such-and-such a house of work, or such-and-such a town, has guardianship. The first of the two readings in this regard is the correct reading of the one who reads with a kasra on the waw, and that is because God followed that with report of His kingdom and authority, and that whoever He brings down His vengeance on the Day of Resurrection will have no helper on that day. So following that report of His being alone in the kingdom and authority is more appropriate than the report of the allegiance that was not mentioned or had any meaning, because of the saying of the one who said: God’s authority is not called guardianship, but rather it is called the authority of human beings, because guardianship means that He is in charge of the affairs of His creation alone without all of His creation, not that He will be a prince over them. They also differed in the reading of His statement the truth. The majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq read it in the accusative case, based on the explanation that it is from the attributes of God, and that the meaning of the statement is: There is the guardianship of God, the Truth, His divinity, not the falsehood of His lengthy divinity which the polytheists call gods. Some of the people of Basra and some of the later Kufians read it God, the Truth in the nominative case, based on their explanation that it is from the attributes of guardianship, and its meaning is: There is the true guardianship, not the falsehood of God alone, with no partner for Him. The first of the two readings in my opinion is correct in that, the reading of those who read it in the accusative case based on the explanation that it is from the attributes of God, and that its meaning is what was described according to the reading of those who read it like that. And His statement, It is better in reward, means that the Almighty says: It is better for those who repent in this life and the next in reward, and it is better in consequence, meaning: “And it is better for them in consequence in the next life when the one who obeys Him, who does what God has commanded him, and who refrains from what God has forbidden him, reaches it. And the consequence is the end. It is said: the consequence of such-and-such a matter, its consequence, and its end, and that is its end and what its end will reach. The readers differed in their reading of this. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as “‘aqba” with a damma on the ‘ayn and a sukoon on the qaf. The statement regarding this, according to us, is that they are two readings that are widespread in the reading of the regions with one meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
18:45: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And give an example of these arrogant ones who said to you: Drive away from you those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, if We bring you the world, from them? He says: An example. Like water which We send down from the sky. He says: Like rain which We send down from the sky. Then the vegetation of the earth mingles with it. He says: So the vegetation of the earth mingles with the water. Then it becomes dry and crumbled. “The winds scatter it.” He says: The winds blow it away and scatter it. It is said: The wind scatters it, scatters it, and scatters it, scatters it, as the poet said: I said to him, Aim and do not strain him, lest he slip from the other end of the stone and you slip. It is said: I threw the man off the beast or camel: if you threw him off. And His saying, And God has power over all things, means: God was able to destroy the garden of this speaker when he entered his garden, I do not think that this will ever perish, and I do not think that the Hour will come, and to destroy the wealth of the miserly with it, in order to remove the worldly life of the disbelievers in Him from them, and other than that which He wills, He is able. Nothing He wills is beyond His power, and nothing He wills exhausts Him. He says: So let the wealthy person not boast about his abundance of wealth, nor act arrogantly toward others because of it, nor let the people of the world be deceived by their worldly life, for its likeness is like this plant that has grown well with the rain, and as soon as the water stops, and its end comes to an end, it returns dry, blown away by the winds, corrupt, and the eyes of those who see it turn away from it. But let him work for the everlasting that does not perish, and the everlasting that does not perish or change.
18:46: God the Almighty says: O people, wealth and children, which Uyaynah and Al-Aqra' boast about, and which they act arrogantly towards Salman, Khabbab and Suhaib, are among the things that adorn themselves with in this life, and are not counted among the Hereafter. And the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord as reward. He says: And what Salman, Khabbab and Suhaib do of obedience to God, and their supplication to their Lord morning and evening seeking His countenance, which remain for them of righteous deeds after the passing of this life, is better, O Muhammad, with your Lord as reward than the wealth and children that these polytheists boast about, which will pass away and will not remain for their people. And better as hope. He says: And what Salman, Suhaib and Khabbab hope for from that is better than what Uyaynah and Al-Aqra' hope for from their wealth and children. And these verses - from His saying: And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord to this point, it was mentioned that they were revealed about Uyaynah and Al-Aqra'. Who said that? Al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Azdi, who was the reciter of al-Azd, on the authority of Abu al-Kanud, on the authority of Khabbab, regarding his statement: And do not repel those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, then he mentioned the story that we mentioned in Surat al-An`am in the story of `Uyaynah and al-Aqra`, until his statement: And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, he said: `Uyaynah and al-Aqra`, and follows his desire, he said: Then he said: He gave them an example of two men, and the example of the life of this world. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the lasting good deeds, as they differed about the meaning of the supplication with which God Almighty described those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade expelling and ordered him to be patient with them. Some of them said: It is the five daily prayers. Some of them said: It is the remembrance of God through glorification, sanctification, and declaration of His oneness, and the like. Some of them said: It is working in obedience to God. Some of them said: Good speech. Mention of those who said: It is the five daily prayers. Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Anmati told me: Yaqub bin Kasib told us: Abdullah bin Abdullah Al-Umawi told us: I heard Abdullah bin Yazid bin Hormuz narrating on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: The lasting righteous deeds are the five daily prayers. Zurayq bin Ishaq told me: Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, and the lasting good deeds, he said: the five daily prayers. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Shurahbil, regarding this verse: And the lasting good deeds, he said: They are the prescribed prayers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The lasting righteous deeds are the five daily prayers. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The lasting good deeds are the five daily prayers. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah: And the lasting good deeds he said: the five daily prayers. Mention of those who said: They are the remembrance of God through glorification, praise, and the like. Ibn Humayd, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad, and Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told us: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Haywah told us: Abu Aqil Zuhra bin Ma’bad Al-Qurashi from Banu Taym from the people of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq told us that he heard Al-Harith, the freed slave of Uthman bin Affan, say: Uthman was asked: What are the lasting good deeds? He said: They are: There is no god but God, Glory be to God, Praise be to God, God is Great, and there is no might nor power except with God. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Abu Zur’ah told us: Haywah told us: Abu Aqil Zuhra bin Ma’bad told us that he heard Al-Harith, the client of Uthman bin Affan, say: It was said to Uthman bin Affan: What are the lasting good deeds? He said: They are: There is no god but God, Glory be to God and His praise, God is greatest, Praise be to God, and there is no might nor power except with God. Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Nafi’ ibn Yazid and Rashdin ibn Sa’d told us: Zuhra ibn Ma’bad told us: I heard al-Harith, the freed slave of Uthman ibn Affan, say: They said to Uthman: What are the lasting good deeds? And he mentioned something similar. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Hormuz, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and the lasting good deeds, he said: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and the lasting good deeds, he said: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Abu Kuraib told us: Talq bin Ghannam told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Malik told us, on the authority of Amara ibn Abdullah ibn Sayyad, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The lasting good deeds are: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power or strength except with God. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim informed me, on the authority of Nafi’ bin Sarjis, that he informed him that he asked Ibn Umar about the lasting good deeds, he said: There is no god but God, and God is the greatest, and glory be to God, and there is no power and no strength except with God. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said something similar. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The lasting good deeds are: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and the lasting good deeds, he said: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abu Sakhr told me: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman, the client of Salim bin Abdul-Dawud, told him: Salim bin Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi sent me and said: Tell him to meet me at the corner of the grave, for I have a need of you. He said: So they met, and one of them greeted the other, then Salim said: How do you count the lasting good deeds? He said: There is no god but God, and praise be to God, and glory be to God, and God is the Greatest, and there is no power and no strength except with God. Salim said to him: When did you include there is no power and no strength except with God in it? He said: I have not ceased to include it. He said: He asked him twice or three times, but he did not give up. He said: Then be steadfast. Salim said: Yes, be steadfast, for Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I was taken up to the heaven and I was shown to Ibrahim, and he said: O Gabriel, who is this with you? He said: Muhammad. He welcomed me and made it easy. Then he said: Tell your nation to plant many plants in Paradise, for its soil is good and its land is spacious. I said: What are the plants in Paradise? He said: There is no power or strength except with God. I found in my book on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Al-Sabah Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Abu Nasr Al-Tammar, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Muslim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest, from the lasting good deeds. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatada, regarding his statement, And the lasting good deeds are better, he said: There is no god but God, God is greatest, praise be to God, and glory be to God, these are the lasting good deeds. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told us, that Diraaj Abu al-Samh told him, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Increase the lasting good deeds. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The religion. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: Allahu Akbar, “La ilaha illa God,” Tasbih, “Al-Hamdulillah,” and There is no power or strength except with God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Malik told me, on the authority of Amara bin Sayyad, that he heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say about the lasting good deeds: They are the servant’s saying: God is Great, Glory be to God, Praise be to God, and there is no power or strength except with God. Ibn Al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Yahya bin Ayoub told us: Ibn Ajlan told me, on the authority of Ammarah bin Sayyad: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab asked me about the lasting good deeds, so I said: Prayer and fasting. He said: You are not right. I said: Zakat and Hajj. He said: You are not right, but they are the five words: There is no god but God, God is the Greatest, Glory be to God, Praise be to God, and There is no power and no strength except with God. He mentioned those who said: It is working in obedience to God, the Almighty. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the lasting righteous deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for hope. He said: The righteous deeds: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the lasting good deeds, he said: They are the remembrance of God, saying, There is no god but God, “God is Great,” Glory be to God, “Praise be to God,” Blessed be God, “There is no power or strength except with God,” I seek forgiveness from God, and may God bless the Messenger of God, as well as fasting, prayer, Hajj, charity, manumission, jihad, maintaining ties of kinship, and all good deeds. They are the lasting good deeds, which will remain for their people in Paradise as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the lasting righteous deeds are better in the sight of your Lord for reward and better for hope, he said: The righteous deeds. He mentioned those who said: They are good words. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the lasting good deeds, he said: Good speech. The most correct of the statements on this is the statement of the one who said: They are all good deeds, like what was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, because all of that is from the good deeds that remain for their doer in the Hereafter, and for them he is rewarded and compensated, and God Almighty did not specify in His statement, And the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord for reward, some over others in the Book, nor in a report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If someone thinks that this is specific to the report that we narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then this is contrary to what he thought, because the report on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that all of it was reported that saying: Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, are among the lasting good deeds, and he did not say: They are all the lasting good deeds, nor all the lasting good deeds, and it is possible that these lasting deeds, and other righteous deeds, are also lasting good deeds.
18:47: God Almighty says, And the Day We remove the mountains from the earth, and We crush them and make them scattered dust. And you see the earth exposed apparent, and its appearance to the eyes of the onlookers without anything covering it of mountain or tree is its emergence. A group of the people of interpretation said something similar to that. Those who said that mentioned: 23109 - Muhammad bin Umar told me and he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa' told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid. And you see the earth exposed he said: There is no wine in it, nor a cave, nor a building, nor a stone in it. Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us. He said: Yazid told us. He said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And you will see the earth barren, with no buildings or trees on it. It was said that the meaning of that is: And you will see the earth barren with its people who were in its belly, then they are on its back. And his statement, And We will gather them, means: We will gather them together to the place of reckoning with Him, and We will not leave behind a single one of them. He says: We will not leave behind, and We will not leave any of them under the earth. It is said from this: I did not leave behind a single one of the people, and I did not betray a single one of them. And from I betrayed is the saying of the rajaz poet: Do you have a partner who is capable of attacking you in a way that will be treacherous to the one who holds it?
18:48: And His statement, And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, the Almighty says: And the creation will be presented before your Lord, O Muhammad, in rows. Indeed, you have come to Us as We created you the first time, the Almighty says: It will be said to them when they are presented to God: You have come to Us, O people, alive as you were when We created you the first time. And the word it was omitted from the statement so that the listeners would know that it is intended in the statement. And His statement, Rather, you claimed that We will not make an appointment for you, this statement was taken as a report from God addressing everyone, and what is intended by it is specific, and that is because a creation of prophets and messengers, and believers in God and His messengers and in the Resurrection may come to the Resurrection. And it is known that it will not be said on that day to those who come to it from the people who believe in God's promise in this world, and the people of certainty in it regarding the establishment of the Hour: Rather, you claimed that We will not make an appointment for you for the Resurrection after death, and the gathering to the Resurrection, and that this is only said to those who in this world denied the Resurrection and the establishment of the Hour.
18:49: May God Almighty say: And on that Day God will place the book of the deeds of His servants in their hands, so one will take it with his right hand and one will take it with his left. Then you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it. God Almighty says: Then you will see the criminals who associate partners with God fearful. He says: Fearful and apprehensive of what is written in it of their evil deeds that they did in this world, lest they be held accountable for them. “And they will say, ‘Woe to us! What is this book that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has recorded it?’” Meaning that they will say when they read their book and see what has been written against them in it of their minor and major sins, they will cry out in woe when they are certain of God’s punishment and are in a state of turmoil because of what they have known of their evil deeds that their book has recorded, and they were not able to deny their correctness. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, What is this Book that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has recorded it? The people complained as you hear the counting, and no one complained unjustly. So beware of small sins, for they accumulate on their doer until they destroy him. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give an example of them, saying: Like the example of a people who set out on a journey until they stopped in a deserted area, and the people’s gathering was attended, and each man set out to collect firewood, so one man would bring a stick and another would bring a stick, until they had gathered a great deal of blackness and lit a fire, for a small sin accumulates on its doer until it destroys him. It was said that what he meant by small in this place is laughter. Those who said that were mentioned: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Abdullah bin Dawud told us, he said: Muhammad bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-Ziyal bin Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He does not leave out a small or a big thing, he said: laughter. Ahmad bin Hazim told us: My father told us: My mother Hamada bint Muhammad told me: I heard my father Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman say about this verse in the statement of God the Almighty: What is this Book that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has recorded it? He said: Small is laughter. And what he means by his statement: What is this Book?: What is the matter with this Book? It leaves out nothing small or great He says: It does not leave out anything small of our sins and deeds or anything large of them but that it has recorded it He says: except that it has preserved it. And they will find whatever they did in this world of deeds present in their book, written and recorded, so they will reward the bad with the like of it, and the good is what God will reward them with. And your Lord does not wrong anyone He says: And your Lord does not reward anyone, O Muhammad, with anything other than what he deserves. He does not reward for good except the people of good, and for evil except the people of evil, and that is justice.
18:50: God Almighty says, reminding these polytheists of the envy of Iblis towards their father and teacher, and what he did of his arrogance and haughtiness towards him when he ordered him to prostrate to him, and that he had enmity and envy towards them for the same thing he had towards their father: And remember, O Muhammad, when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and they prostrated, except for Iblis, whom these polytheists obey and follow his command, and disobey God’s command, for he did not prostrate to him out of arrogance towards God, and out of envy of Adam. He was from the jinn. The people of interpretation differed in the meaning of His statement, He was from the jinn. Some of them said: He was from a tribe that protected them from the jinn. Others said: Rather, he was from the treasurers of Paradise, so he was attributed to Paradise. Others said: Rather, it was said from the jinn because he was from the jinn who were hidden from the eyes of the children of Adam. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Khallad ibn Ata’, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: His name before he committed the sin was Azazel, and he was one of the inhabitants of the earth, and he was one of the most diligent of the angels and the most knowledgeable of them, so that is what led him to arrogance, and he was from a tribe called Jinn. Abu Kuraib narrated: Uthman ibn Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Bishr ibn Ammarah, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis was from a tribe of angels called the jinn. They were created from the poisonous fire from among the angels, and his name was Al-Harith. He said: He was a treasurer from the treasurers of Paradise. He said: The angels were created from a light other than this tribe. He said: The jinn mentioned in the Qur’an were created from a flame of fire, which is the tongue of fire that is at its edge when it ignites. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Shaiban told us, he said: Salam bin Maskeen told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Iblis was the chief of the angels of the lowest heaven. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Except Iblis, he was from the jinn, he said: Iblis was one of the treasurers of Paradise, and he managed the affairs of the lowest heaven. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Ibn Abbas said: Iblis was one of the noblest of the angels and the most honorable of them in tribe. He was the keeper of Paradise, and he had authority over the lowest heaven and the earth. Among what God decreed was that he saw that he had honor and greatness over the people of Heaven, so arrogance arose in his heart that no one knows except God. So when he was prostrating when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, God extracted his arrogance from the prostration, so He cursed him and postponed him until the Day of Judgment. He said: Ibn Abbas said: His statement, He was from the jinn, is that he was called Paradise because he was its keeper, just as a man is called a Meccan, a Medinan, a Kufan, or a Basran. Ibn Jurayj said this. Others said: They are a tribe of angels, a tribe, and the name of his tribe was the jinn. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Salih, the freed slave of Al-Tawamah, and Sharik Ibn Abi Namir, one of them or both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Among the angels is a tribe of jinn, And Iblis was among them, and he used to rule what was between heaven and earth, but he disobeyed, so God became angry with him and transformed him into a cursed devil. May God curse him as he was transformed. He said: If a man’s sin was due to arrogance, then do not expect him. But if his sin was due to disobedience, then expect him. Adam’s sin was due to disobedience, and Iblis’ sin was due to arrogance. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was one of the jinn,” is a tribe of angels called the jinn. Ibn Abbas said: If he had not been one of the angels, he would not have been commanded to prostrate, and he was in charge of the treasury of the lowest heaven. He said: Qatada used to say: He went crazy from obeying his Lord. Al-Hasan used to say: God forced him to return to his lineage. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Except Iblis, he was from the jinn, he said: He was from a tribe of angels called the jinn. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Iblis was never among the angels for even a moment, and he is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam, peace be upon him, is the origin of mankind. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Iblis was over the lowest heaven and over the earth and the keeper of Paradise. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, So they prostrated themselves, except for Iblis, he was from the jinn, Ibn Abbas used to say: Iblis was from the noblest of the angels and the most honorable of their tribe, and he was the guardian of Paradise, and he had authority over the lowest heaven and authority over the earth, and among the things that his soul suggested to him from the decree of God was that he saw that he had honor over the people of the heavens, so arrogance occurred in his heart that no one knows except God, so God extracted that arrogance from him when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, but he was arrogant and was from the disbelievers, so that is what He said to the angels, Indeed, I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal, meaning: what Iblis concealed in his soul of arrogance. And his saying, He was from the jinn, Ibn Abbas used to say: God said, He was from the jinn, because he was a keeper of the heavens, just as a man is called a Meccan, a Medinan, a Basran, or a Kufan. Others said: The name of Iblis’ tribe was the jinn, and they are a tribe of angels called the jinn, so God Almighty said, He was from the jinn, so He attributed him to his tribe. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, regarding his statement, He was from the jinn, he said: From the jinn who work in the gardens. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Saeed Al-Yahmadi Ismail bin Ibrahim told us: Suwar bin Al-Ja’d Al-Yahmadi told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, regarding his statement, of the jinn, he said: Iblis was one of the jinn whom the angels expelled, so some of the angels captured him and took him to heaven. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Except Iblis, he was one of the jinn and disobeyed the command of his Lord, he said: He was the keeper of Paradise, so he was called Paradise. Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi told me: Ahmad ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Abi al-Miqdam, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: Iblis was one of the keepers of Paradise. We have already explained the statement on this in what has preceded in this book of ours, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed on it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement, So he disobeyed the command of his Lord, means: So he went against the command of his Lord, deviated from it and deviated, as Ru`bah said: They wander in Najd and are deeply wicked and unjust. A: By fawasiq means: the camels that deviate from the straight path of Najd, and likewise, fawasiq in religion is only deviation from the straight path and deviation from righteousness. It is narrated from the Arabs by hearing: Fawasiq means that the date fawasiq means that it came out of its shell, and fawasiq means that the mouse fawasiq means that it came out of its hole. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: Fawasiq ‘an amr Rabbih was said because it means that he fawasiq means that he rejected the command of God, just as the Arabs say: Atakhmat ‘an al-ta’im meaning: I was gorged on eating. We have already explained the statement about that, and that its meaning is: He deviated and went against the command of God, and deviated from it. Some scholars of the Arabic language said: The meaning of fawasiq is excessiveness. He claimed that the Arabs say: Fawasiq fi al-nafqah means that he was excessive in it. He said: The fasiq was called fasiq because of his excess in what God has forbidden. And the scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad bin Omar told us, and he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, Then he disobeyed the command of his Lord, he said: Regarding prostration to Adam. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Mujahid narrated: Concerning His statement, Then he disobeyed the command of his Lord, he said: He disobeyed in prostrating to Adam. And His statement, Then would you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are enemies to you? God Almighty says: “O children of Adam, would you take him who was arrogant towards your father and envied him and denied My blessings upon him, and deceived him until I expelled him from Paradise and the comfort of his life therein to the earth and the hardship of life therein, and you obey him and his descendants instead of God despite his enmity towards you in the past and present, and you abandon the obedience of your Lord who bestowed blessings upon you and honored you by making His angels prostrate to your father, and making him dwell in His gardens, and giving you from the abundance of His blessings what cannot be counted in number?” And the temptation of Iblis: the devils who tempt the children of Adam. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me? He said: His offspring are the devils, and he counted them as: Zalnabur, the master of the markets, who would place his banner in every market between heaven and earth, and Thabar, the master of calamities, and the one-eyed, the master of fornication, and Masut, the master of report, who would bring it and throw it into the mouths of the people, and they would find no basis for it, and Dasim, who, if a man entered his house and did not greet him and did not mention God, would see the goods that were not raised, and if he ate and did not mention the name of God, he would eat with him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, he said: I heard Al-A’mash say: If I enter the house and I have not converted to Islam, I see a woman who is ablution, so I say: Lift up, lift up, and I argue with them, then I remember and say: Dasim Dasim. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They are four: Thabr, Dasim, Zalnabur, Al-Awar, and Masut: one of them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me? And they reproduce as the children of Adam reproduce, and they are your enemies. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Then would you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are enemies to you? He is the father of the jinn just as Adam was the father of mankind. And he said: God said to Satan: I will not create for Adam any descendants except that I will create for you the like thereof. So there is no one among the children of Adam who does not have a devil attached to him. And His statement, What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers, the Almighty says: What an evil exchange for the disbelievers in God is to take Iblis and his offspring as allies instead of God, and they are your enemies because they abandoned taking God as an ally by following His commands and prohibitions, and He is the One who bestowed blessings upon them and upon their father Adam before them, and bestowed upon them countless favors, as an exchange. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Thanayzid, he said: Thanasa’id, on the authority of Qatada: What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers! What an evil exchange! They exchanged the worship of their Lord for obeying Satan.
18:51: The Almighty said: I did not make Iblis and his offspring witness the creation of the heavens and the earth meaning: I did not make them witness that so that I could seek their help in creating them nor the creation of themselves meaning: I did not make some of them witness the creation of some of them so that I could seek their help in creating them, rather I was unique in creating all of that without any helper or supporter, meaning: So how did they take their enemy as allies instead of Me, while they are a creation of the likes of their creation, and they abandoned My worship while I am the One who bestowed favors upon them and upon their ancestors, and their Creator and the Creator of those whom they befriend instead of Me, alone in that without any helper or supporter. His saying, And I would not have taken those who lead astray as helpers, means: I would not have taken those who do not guide to the truth, but rather lead astray, so whoever follows them deviates from the straight path, as helpers and supporters. It is from their saying: So-and-so supports so-and-so if he strengthens and aids him. Some of the interpreters said something similar. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And I would not have taken the misguiders as assistants: meaning, helpers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. What he meant by that is that Satan and his followers lead the children of Adam astray from the truth and do not guide them to the right path. It may also be possible that he meant the misguiders who are followers in misguidance and companions who are not guided.
18:52: God the Almighty says: And on the Day when He will say God the Almighty to those who associate others with Him, Call upon My partners whom you claimed He will say to them: Call upon those whom you claimed were My partners in worship to support you and protect you from Me. So they called upon them, but they did not respond to them He says: So they sought help from them, but they did not help them. And We placed between them a place of destruction. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And We placed between these polytheists and what they used to call upon besides God, partners in this world, enmity on that Day. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, And We have placed between them a cause of destruction, he said: He has placed enmity between them on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Bashar told us: Uthman ibn Umar told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And We placed between them a cause of destruction. He said: Enmity. Others said: Its meaning is: And We made their action a cause of destruction for them. Mention of those who said that: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We placed between them a cause of destruction, he said: a cause of destruction. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, destructive, he said: destruction. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We placed between them a cause of destruction, he said: The cause of destruction is the destroyer, in which some of them destroyed others, some of them destroyed others. And he recited: And We have set a time for their destruction. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Mubqan means destruction. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Urfajah, regarding His statement, And We placed between them a place of destruction, he said: a place of destruction. Others said: It is the name of a valley in Hell. Those who said that were mentioned: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Amr al-Bakali: And We placed between them a barrier. He said: A deep valley that separated the people of misguidance from the people of guidance, and the people of Paradise from the people of Hell. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We placed between them a barrier of destruction. It was mentioned to us that Amr al-Bakali told on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: It is a deep valley through which the people of guidance will be separated on the Day of Resurrection from the people of misguidance. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Artah, he said: Mujahid said, And We placed between them a barrier, he said: A valley in the Fire. Muhammad bin Omar told us, and he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And We placed between them a place of destruction, he said: A valley in Hell.
