However, I choose to read it with a shaddah on the ta’ of la-ta’ala, because it is the more eloquent and famous of the two dialects, and the one most often used by the Arabs.
18:78: God Almighty says: The companion of Moses said to Moses: What you said, which is His statement, If you had willed, you could have taken payment for it, “is a separation between me and you,” meaning: a separation between me and you: meaning a separation between me and you. Shall I inform you? He says: I will tell you the interpretation of that which you could not have patience for? He says: what the consequences of my actions that I knew would lead to, so you could not have patience to stop asking about them and to stop criticizing me for them. And God knows best.
18:79: He says: As for what I did to the ship, it was because it belonged to poor people who worked at sea, so I wanted to damage it with the holes I made in it. As Ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, So I wanted to fault it, he said: I would tear it apart. Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And his saying, And behind them was a king who seized every ship by force, and in front of them and ahead of them was a king. As Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, And behind them was a king. Qatada said: In front of them. Do you not see that he says, Behind them is Hell, and it is in front of them? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was in the recitation: And before them was a king who seized every intact ship by force. And it was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited that: And before them was a king. Abu Jaafar said: Some of the people who know the Arabic language have made raa one of the letters of opposites, and he claimed that it refers to what is in front of it and what is behind it, and he cited as evidence for the validity of that the words of the poet: I hope that the Banu Marwan will listen to me and obey me, and my people Tamim and the desert behind them Meaning in front of me, and he has overlooked the correct aspect of that. Rather, what is in front of him is said: He is behind me, because you are behind him. So you will meet him as he will meet you, so it became: when he was meeting you, it was as if he was behind you and you were in front of him. Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa did not allow it to be said to a man in front of you: he is behind me, nor if he was behind you to be said: he is in front of me, and he said: this is only permissible in times of days and times like the saying of the one who says: behind you is severe cold, and in front of you is severe heat, because you are behind it, so it was permissible because it is something that comes, so it is as if if it catches up with you it becomes behind you, and as if if you reach it it becomes in front of you. He said: therefore the two meanings are permissible. And his saying: He seizes every ship by force the speaker says: what benefit did this scholar's tearing of the ship he boarded from its people, since because of its tearing he seizes all the ships, defective and non-defective, and what was the reason for his justification for tearing it, that he tearing it, because behind them is a king who seizes every ship by force? It was said: The meaning of this is that he would take every sound ship by force, and leave every defective one, not that he would take the sound ones and the unsound ones. If he says: What is the evidence that this is the case? It was said: His saying, So I wanted to find fault with it, thus made clear that he only found fault with it because the defective ones were not exposed to it, so it was sufficient for it to be said: And behind them was a king who would take every sound ship by force, although this is also the case in some readings. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Mal: It is in the wording of Ibn Masoud: And behind them was a king who seized every good ship by force. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Al-Hasan bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: In my father’s reading: And behind them was a king who seized every good ship by force, and I only blamed it to turn him away from it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And behind them was a king who would seize every ship by force. So when they succeeded him, they would repair it with pitch and enjoy it. Ibn Jurayj said: Wahb ibn Sulayman told me, on the authority of Shu’ayb al-Jubba’i, that the name of the man who would seize every ship by force was Hadad ibn Badad.
18:80: God Almighty says: As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers. So do we know that he would overwhelm them? He says, he would overwhelm them with transgression, which is arrogance towards God and disbelief in Him. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, and it was mentioned in some letters: As for the boy, he was a disbeliever. Mention of those who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: As for the boy, he was a disbeliever in the letter of Abi: And his parents were believers. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to kinship. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And as for the boy, his parents were believers. And he was a disbeliever in some readings. His saying: So we feared. And it is in the Mushaf of Abdullah: So your Lord feared that He would overburden them with transgression and disbelief. Amr ibn Ali told us: Abu Qutaybah told us: Abdul-Jabbar ibn Abbas al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The boy whom al-Khidr killed was marked as an unbeliever on the day he was marked. The Arabs direct fear and dread to the meaning of suspicion, and these letters are directed to the meaning of knowledge of something that is perceived through something other than the senses and sight. We have explained that with its evidence in other places, so there is no need to repeat it. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: The meaning of his saying we feared in this place is: we hated, because God is not feared. And he said in some of the readers: So fear your Lord. He said: It is like the two men feared that they would be dependent, and he does not fear that more than he hates it for them.
18:81: And His statement, So We intended that their Lord should substitute them: The reciters differed in the recitation of that, so a group of the reciters of Mecca, Medina, and Basra recited it, So We intended that their Lord should substitute them. Some of them used to justify the validity of that by saying that it was found stressed in most of the Qur'an, like the statement of God, the Almighty, So those who wronged substituted, and His statement, And when We substituted a verse for another verse: so the correct statement is, So We intended that He should substitute them with it. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited that, So We intended that He should substitute them with a light dal. Some of those who recited that in the same way from the people of Arabic said: Abdal yabdal with a light dal and badal yabdal with a heavy dal have the same meaning. The correct thing to say about this in my opinion is that they are two readings with similar meanings. A group of reciters have recited each of them, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. It has been said that God Almighty replaced the parents of the boy whom Moses’ companion killed with a girl. Those who said this: Yaqub told me, he said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Mubarak bin Saeed told us, he said: Amr bin Qais told us regarding His statement, So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to kinship. He said: It has reached me that she is a girl. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Sulayman ibn Umayyah told me that he heard Yaqub ibn Asim say: They replaced the boy with a girl. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim told me that he heard Saeed ibn Jubayr say: They replaced the boy with a girl. Others said: Their Lord replaced them with a Muslim boy. Mention of those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to kinship. He said: His mother was pregnant at that time with a Muslim boy. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that he mentioned the boy whom Al-Khidr killed, and he said: His parents were happy with him when he was born and grieved for him when he was killed, and if he had lived, it would have led to their destruction. So let a person be satisfied with the decree of God, for God’s decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree in what he likes. And his saying, Better than him in zakat, means: Better than the boy he killed in terms of righteousness and religion. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity, he said: Islam. And his saying, and closer in kinship, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: and closer in mercy to his parents and more dutiful to them than the one who was killed. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada: And the closest of kin means the most pious to him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And closer to kinship, meaning closer to goodness. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It is more likely that his parents will have mercy on him than the one who was killed. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And closer in kinship means more merciful to him than they were to the one who killed Al-Khidr. Some of the Arab scholars interpreted that as: And closer to have mercy on him. Womb is the source of mercy. It is said: I had mercy on him with mercy and compassion. Some of the Basrans used to say: From womb and kinship. And it may be said: womb and womb like ‘asr and ‘asr, and halaka and halaka. And he cited as evidence for his statement the verse of Al-Ajjaj: And the womb of those who are crooked is not crooked There is no point in the womb in this context, because the murdered person was the one whose parents God replaced with a son for the murdered person’s parents, so their kinship to his parents and their kinship to him in the womb are the same. Rather, the meaning of that is: And it is closer to the murdered person that he shows mercy to his parents and is dutiful to them, as Qatada said. The statement may be directed to its meaning being: And it is closer to them showing mercy to him, but no one among the people of interpretation interpreted it in this way, so since there is no one who interpreted it, then what we said is correct in it, for what we have explained.
18:82: God Almighty says, informing us about the words of Moses’ companion: As for the wall that I erected, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was a treasure beneath it for them. The people of interpretation differed about that treasure, and some of them said: It was scrolls containing buried knowledge. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And beneath it was a treasure for them. He said: There was a treasure of knowledge beneath it. Yaqub told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, And beneath it was a treasure for them. He said: It was a treasure of knowledge. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, And there was a treasure under it for them. He said: Knowledge. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Dawud told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, And there was a treasure under it for them. He said: Knowledge. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And there was beneath it a treasure for them, he said: scrolls for two boys in which there was knowledge. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The pages of knowledge. Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghafari told me: Hanada bint Malik Al-Shaibaniyyah told us: I heard my friend Hammad bin Al-Walid Al-Thaqafi say: I heard Jaafar bin Muhammad say about the statement of God Almighty: And beneath it was a treasure for them both. He said: Two lines and a half, the third was not completed: I am amazed at the one who is certain of provision how he tires himself, and I am amazed at the one who is certain of the reckoning how he is heedless, and I am amazed at the one who is certain of death how he rejoices when He said: And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as reckoners. She said: It was mentioned that they were preserved by the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness was mentioned from them, and between them and the father by whom they were preserved were seven fathers, who was a weaver. Yaqub told me, he said: Al-Hasan bin Habeemb bin Nadbah told us, he said: Salamah bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Na’im al-Anbari, who was one of Al-Hasan’s companions, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say, regarding His statement, And beneath it was a treasure for them both, he said: A golden tablet on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful: I am amazed at the one who believes, how he can grieve, and I am amazed at the one who is certain of death, how he can rejoice, and I am amazed at the one who knows the world and its vicissitudes with its people, how he can be reassured by it. There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ammarah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And there was beneath it a treasure for them, he said, Pages of knowledge. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn told us, he said: Abdullah bin Ayyash told me, on the authority of Omar, the freed slave of Ghafra, he said: The treasure that God said in the Surah in which the cave is mentioned, And beneath it was a treasure for them, he said: It was a solid gold tablet, on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I am amazed at someone who knew death and then laughed. I am amazed at someone who was certain of destiny and then became weary. I am amazed at someone who was certain of death and then felt secure. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Others said: Rather, it was hidden wealth. Those who said that mentioned: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Ikrimah: And there was a treasure beneath it for them. He said: A treasure. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ikrimah, the same. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Abu Husayn told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, something similar. Shu’bah said: We did not hear it from him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: And beneath it was a treasure for them. He said: It was money for them. Qatada said: The treasure was made permissible for those who came before us, and forbidden for us. For God makes permissible whatever He wills of His command, and forbids, and they are the Sunnahs and the obligatory duties. He makes permissible for one nation and forbids for another, but God does not accept from anyone who has passed away except sincerity and monotheism for Him. The first of the two interpretations is the correct one: the statement made by Ikrimah, because it is known from the speech of the Arabs that the treasure is the name for whatever is hoarded of money, and that everything that is hoarded has the name treasure applied to it. So the interpretation is diverted to the most common usage of those addressed by the revelation, unless there is evidence that requires diverting it to something else, for reasons that we have explained in more than one place. And His statement, And their father was Salih, and your Lord intended that they should reach maturity, means: So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and strength and then extract their treasure hidden under the wall that you had erected, out of mercy from your Lord for them. He says: You did this to the wall, out of mercy from your Lord for the orphans. And Ibn Abbas used to say about that what: Musa bin Abdul Rahman told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Maysarah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said, in his statement, And their father was righteous, he said: They were preserved by the righteousness of their father, and what was mentioned of their righteousness. Abu Kuraib told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. And his statement, And I did not do it of my own accord, means: And I did not do, O Moses, all that you saw me do of my own accord, and of my own accord. Rather, I did it based on God’s command to me. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I did not do it of my own accord. He was a servant who was commanded, so he carried out God’s command. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And what I did of my own accord means I have not seen anything that I did of my own accord. And His statement: That is the interpretation of that over which you were not able to have patience means: What is the interpretation of what I mentioned to you of the reasons for which I did the actions that you found reprehensible from me? He says: What is the interpretation of the actions that you were not able to leave off asking Me about and your denouncing them with patience? These stories that God Almighty told His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Moses and his companion, are a lesson from Him to him, and a warning to him to stop hastening the punishment of the polytheists who denied Him and mocked Him and His Book, and an announcement from Him to him that His actions towards them, even if they happened as the eyes see, in a way that might sometimes happen to His friends, their interpretation leads them to the conditions of His enemies in them, just as the actions of Moses’ companion were contrary to what appeared to be correct in Moses’s eyes, since he was not aware of their consequences, while they were correct in reality and would eventually lead to the truth. The correctness of that is indicated by His statement: “And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Merciful. If He were to impose blame on them for what they have earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. Rather, for them is an appointed time from which they will not find any refuge.” Then he followed that with the story of Moses and his companion, teaching his prophet that his leaving the punishment of these polytheists to be hastened, without looking at them, even if that is what one who has no knowledge of what God has planned for them thinks, is looking at them, because the interpretation of that leads to their destruction and ruin by the sword in this world and their deserving of eternal disgrace from God in the Hereafter.
18:83: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And these polytheists ask you, O Muhammad, about Dhul-Qarnayn, what was his affair and what was his story. So say to them: I will recite to you a mention of his story. He says: I will relate to you a story about him. It has been said that those who asked the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, about the affair of Dhul-Qarnayn were people from the People of the Book. As for the report that those who asked him about that were polytheists from his people, we have mentioned it before. As for the report that those who asked him were people of the Book: Abu Kuraib narrated it to us. He said: Zaid bin Habbab narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah. He said: Abd al-Rahman bin Ziyad bin An’am narrated to us on the authority of two sheikhs from Tajib. One of them said to his companion: Let us go to Uqbah bin Amir so that we may talk. They said: So they went to him and said: We have come so that you may talk to us. He said: One day I was serving the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I left him and some people from the People of the Book met me. They said: We want to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He asked permission for us to see him, so I entered upon him and told him. He said: What do I have to do with them? I have no knowledge except what God has taught me. Then he said: Pour me some water. So he performed ablution and prayed. He said: Before he finished, I could see the joy on his face. Then he said: Bring them in to me, and whoever you see of my companions. So they entered and stood before him. He said: If you wish, you may ask, and I will tell you what you find written in your book, and if you wish, I will tell you. They said: Yes, tell us. He said: You came to ask me about Dhul-Qarnayn, and what you find written in your book. He was a young man from the Romans. He came and built the city of Alexandria in Egypt. When he finished, an angel came to him and lifted him up to the sky. He said to him: What do you see? He said: I see my city and cities. Then he ascended with him. He said: What do you see? He said: I see my city. Then he ascended with him and said: What do you see? He said: I see the earth. He said: This sea surrounds the world. Indeed, God has sent me to you to teach the ignorant and to confirm the knowledgeable. So he brought him the dam, which is two soft mountains that everything slips from. Then he went with him until he passed Gog and Magog. Then he went with him to another nation, their faces are the faces of dogs fighting Gog and Magog. Then he went with him until he cut off another nation fighting those whose faces are the faces of dogs. Then he went with him until he cut off these to another nation that he named. The scholars differed about the meaning for which Dhul-Qarnayn was called Dhul-Qarnayn. Some of them said: He was called that because he was struck on his horn and perished, then he was revived and struck on the other horn and perished. Those who said that mentioned: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyil, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he said: He is a servant who loved God and He loved him, and he advised God and He advised him, so he commanded them to fear God, so they struck him on his horn and killed him, then God resurrected him, so they struck him on his horn and he died. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he said: He was a servant who advised God and God advised him. He called his people to God, and they struck him on his horn and he died, but God revived him. He called his people to God, and they struck him on his horn and he died, so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyal, who said: I heard Ali, and they asked him about Dhul-Qarnayn: Was he a prophet? He said: He was a righteous servant who loved God and God loved him, and he advised God and God advised him. Then God sent him to his people, and they struck him twice on the head, so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn, and there is someone like him among you today. Others said about that as follows: Muhammad bin Sahl al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: Ismail bin Abdul Karim narrated to us, saying: Abdul Samad bin Maqal narrated to us, saying: Wahb bin Munabbih said: Dhul-Qarnayn was a king. It was said to him: Why was he called Dhul-Qarnayn? He said: The People of the Book differed concerning him. Some of them said: The king of the Romans and Persians. Some of them said: He had something like two horns on his head. Others said: He was called that because the two sides of his head were made of copper. Those who said that are mentioned: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told us: Someone I do not accuse told me on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani: He was called Dhul-Qarnayn because the two sides of his head were made of copper.
18:84: And His statement, Indeed, We established him upon the earth and gave him from every thing a means, means: We established him upon the earth. And We gave him from every thing a means, means: We gave him from every thing: meaning what leads to it, which is knowledge of it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We gave him a reason for everything, meaning: knowledge. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We gave him a reason for everything: meaning knowledge. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And We gave him a reason for everything, he said: Knowledge of everything. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, And We gave him a reason for everything, he said: knowledge of everything. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We gave him a reason for everything knowledge. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We gave him a cause for everything, meaning: knowledge.
18:85: And his saying, So he followed a path. The readers differed in their reading of that. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it as so he followed with the alif connected and the ta' doubled, meaning: he walked and traveled, from the saying of the speaker: I followed the trace of so-and-so: if I followed him and walked behind him. The majority of Kufa readers read it as Fataba’a with a hamza on the alif and a light ta’, meaning caught up. The first of the two readings in this regard is the correct reading: the reading of the one who read it as fa-taba’a with the alif connected and the ta’ doubled, because this is report from God Almighty about the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn in the land in which he was empowered, not about his reaching the cause, and this is how the interpretation of the people of interpretation came. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then he followed a cause, meaning by cause: the home. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement a cause, he said: a home and a path between the east and the west. Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaid God bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: Then he followed a path, he said: A path on the earth. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then he followed a way: he followed the dwellings of the earth and its landmarks. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, Then follow a way, he said: This is now the way of the paths, as Pharaoh said, O Haman, build me a tower that I may reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, he said: The ways of the heavens. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then he followed a way, he said: The dwellings of the earth. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement, Then follow a way, he said: The stations.
18:86: God Almighty says: Until when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a hot spring. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. Some of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it in a hot spring, meaning that it sets in a hot spring of water. A group of the reciters of Medina and most of the reciters of Kufa recited it in a hot spring, meaning that it sets in a hot spring of water. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, just as the reciters differed in their reading of it. He mentioned the one who said, He set in a hot spring. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He found it setting in a murky spring. He said: In black mud. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite in a hot spring. He said: one with hot mud. Al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd narrated to us, saying: Sa`id ibn Muslimah narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Hadir, saying: I heard Abdullah ibn Abbas say: Mu`awiyah recited this verse and said: A hot spring. Ibn Abbas said: It is a hot spring. He said: So they put Ka`b between them. He said: So they sent to Ka`b al-Ahbar and asked him, and Ka`b said: As for the sun, it sets in Tha`t, so it was as Ibn Abbas said, and Tha`t is mud. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Nafi’ ibn Abi Na’im told me, he said: I heard Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj say: Ibn Abbas used to say, in a murky spring, then he explained it as: having murky mud. Nafi’ said: Ka’b was asked about it, and he said: You are more knowledgeable about the Qur’an than I am, but I find it in the Book that it disappears into black mud. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He found it setting in a murky spring. He said: It is the murky water. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: In a hot spring. He said: Tha’t. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, set in a spring of murky water, he said: Tha’ata. He said: Amr bin Dinar informed me, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I read in a hot spring, and Amr bin Al-Aas read in a hot spring. So we sent to Ka’b, and he said: It sets in a hot, black mud. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It sets in a hot spring. Hot spring means black mud. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Marwan bin Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, who said: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say: Ibn Abbas used to recite this letter in a hot spring and say: Black mud in which the sun sets. Others said: Rather, it disappears in a hot spring. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He found it setting in a hot spring. He said: in a hot spring. Yaqub told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Al-Hasan say, In a hot spring. He said: Hot. Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement, in a hot spring, he said: Hot, and al-Hasan read it in this way. The correct thing to say about that, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions, and each one of them has a correct aspect and an understood meaning, and neither of its aspects corrupts the other, and that is because it is possible for the sun to set in a hot spring with hot mud, so the reader would be describing it with the characteristic that it has, which is hot, and the reader would be describing it with the characteristic that it has, which is mud and mud. And it was narrated with both of its forms, which I said are from its characteristics, report. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Al-Awam told us: A client of Abdullah ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the sun when it set and said: In the blazing fire of God, in the blazing fire of God. Were it not for the command of God that restrains it, it would have burned everything on the earth.” Al-Fadl bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told me: Abu Dawud told us: Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Saad bin Aws, on the authority of Musaddaa, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to him Ham’ah. And His statement, And he found there a people, He mentioned that those people were called asik. And His statement, We said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish them,’ He said, “either you kill them if they do not enter into the acknowledgment of the Oneness of God and submit to what you call them to in terms of obeying their Lord. “Or you take good care of them,” He said, or you take them captive and teach them guidance and show them the right path.
18:87: He, the Most High, says: “He said: As for he who does wrong, We will punish him.” He continues: As for he who disbelieves, We will kill him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, But as for him who has wronged, We will punish him, he said: It means killing. And his statement, Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment, he said: Then he will return to God Almighty after being killed, and He will punish him with a great punishment, which is the terrible punishment, and that is the punishment of Hell.
18:88: He says: As for he among them who believed in God and believed in Him alone, and acted in obedience to Him, then for him is the best with God, which is Paradise, as a reward, meaning a recompense for his faith and obedience to his Lord. The reciters differed in the recitation of this, so most of the reciters of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra and Kufa recited it, For him is the best reward, raising the recompense and adding it to the best. If this is recited in this way, then there are two interpretations: One of them is that the best is meant to refer to his faith and righteous deeds, so the meaning of the statement, if this is what is meant by it, is: As for he who believes and does righteous deeds, then for him is its reward, meaning the reward for these good deeds. The second interpretation is that what is meant by the best is Paradise, and the reward is added to it, as it was said, And the home of the Hereafter is better, and the home is the Hereafter, and as it was said, And that is the religion of right, and the religion is the right. Others read: For him is the best reward, meaning: For him is Paradise as a reward. So the reward is in the accusative case as a source, meaning: He will reward them with the reward of Paradise. The more correct of the two readings in this, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read it: For him is the best reward, with the accusative case of the reward and its tanween, according to the meaning that I described, that they will have Paradise as a reward. So the reward is in the accusative case as an explanation. And His statement: And We will speak to him from Our command with ease, means: And We will teach him in this world what is easy for us to teach him, which will bring him closer to God and soften our speech to him. And Mujahid used to say something similar to what we said about that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Of Our command, ease, he said, well-known. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.
18:89: God Almighty says: Then Dhul-Qarnayn proceeded and took paths and stations. As Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then he followed a path, meaning a home. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then he followed a way the houses of the earth and its landmarks.
18:90: Until, when he reached the place of sunrise, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any shield against it. God Almighty says: And Dhul-Qarnayn found the sun rising on a people for whom We had not made any shield against it. This was because their land had no mountains or trees, and could not support buildings, so they lived in houses, but rather sank into the water or crept into the streams. Ibrahim bin Al-Mustamir told me, he said: Sulayman bin Dawud and Abu Dawud told us, they said: Sahl bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Siraj told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: It will rise upon a people for whom We have not made any shelter from it. He said: It was a land that could not support building, and when the sun rose upon them they would sink into the water, and when it set they would come out to graze their flocks, as animals graze. He said: Then Al-Hasan said: This is the hadith of Samurah. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Until, when he reached the place of sunrise, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any shelter against it. He mentioned to us that they were in a place where no building could stand, but rather they would be in groups of theirs, until when the sun had passed their zenith, they would go out to their livelihoods and their fields. He said: Thus, We have encompassed what he had in knowledge. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, And he found it rising upon a people for whom We had not made any shelter besides it, he said: They had never built a building in it, and no building was ever built upon them in it. And when the sun rose upon them, they would enter flocks that had the right to the sun’s descent, or they would enter the sea, because their land had no mountains. And an army came to them once, and its people said to them, Do not let the sun rise upon you while you are in it. They said, We will not leave until the sun rises. What are these bones? They said, These are the corpses of an army upon whom the sun rose here and they died. He said, So they went fleeing in the land. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, It will rise upon a people for whom We have not made any shelter against it, he said: It has reached us that they were in a place where no building could stand, so they would enter into their swarms when the sun rose, until it had set, then they would go out to their livelihoods. Others said: They are the Zanj. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, It will look down upon a people for whom We have not made any shield against it, he said: It is said: They are the Zanj.
18:91: As for his saying likewise, its meaning is: Then he followed a cause likewise, until he reached the rising of the sun. Likewise: from the connection of followed. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: Then he followed a cause, until he reached the rising of the sun, just as he followed a cause until he reached its setting. And his saying, And We have encompassed what he has with knowledge, means: And We have encompassed what is at the rising of the sun with knowledge. Nothing of what is there of creation, their conditions, and their causes, or of others, is hidden from us. And with what we said about the meaning of the report, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement report he said: knowledge. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Likewise, and We have encompassed what he has with knowledge, he said: knowledge.
18:92: God Almighty says: Then he traveled through roads and houses, and took paths.
18:93: God Almighty says: Then he traveled through roads and places, and took paths, until he reached between the two barriers. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as until it reaches bayn al-saddayn with a damma on the seen, and likewise everything in the Qur’an of this type with a damma on the seen. Some of the reciters of Mecca read it with a fatha on all of it. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ used to open the seen in this surah, and closed the seen in Ya-Seen. He used to say: The dam with the fatha is the barrier between you and something, and the dam with the damma is the covering of the eye. As for the Kufians, the majority of their recitation in the entire Qur’an is with a fatha on the seen, except for the statement until it reaches bayn al-saddayn, in which case they closed the seen in particular. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah regarding this, what: Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated to us, he said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Whatever is made by the sons of Adam is the dam, meaning with the fat-ha, and whatever is made by God is the dam. Al-Kisa’i used to say: They are two languages with one meaning. The correct thing to say about that, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions, and two languages that agree on the meaning and do not differ, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct. There is no meaning to the difference that was mentioned by Abu Amr ibn al-Ala and Ikrimah between sadd and sadd, because we did not find any witness to that that clarifies the difference between that according to what was narrated from them. What clarifies that is that all the people of interpretation who narrated to us from them a statement about that, did not narrate to us from any of them a distinction between the fathah and damma of that, and if they differed in meaning, the separation would have been transferred with the interpretation, God willing, but the meaning of that was not separate for them, so the letter is interpreted without a distinction from them between that. As for what was mentioned from Ikrimah about that, the one who narrated that from Ayoub Harun, and there is doubt in his narration, and we do not know that from Ayoub from the narration of his trustworthy companions. The dam and the dam together: the barrier between two things, and here, as mentioned, they are two mountains that blocked what is between them, so Dhul-Qarnayn built a barrier between Yajuj and Majuj and those behind them, to cut off the source of their evil and their chaos from them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Until when he reached between the two barriers, he said: The two mountains are the embankment between Gog and Magog, two nations from behind the embankment of Dhul-Qarnayn. He said: The two mountains are Armenia and Azerbaijan. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Until he reached between the two mountains. They are two mountains. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, between the two barriers, meaning between two mountains. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Between the two dams, he said: They are two mountains. And His saying, And he found, beyond them, a people who could hardly understand a word. The Almighty says: He found, beyond the two barriers, a people who could hardly understand a word other than their own words. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase yafqahunu understanding. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, read it as yafqahunu qawlan with a fatha on the qaf and the ya’, from faqahu al-rajul yafqahu fiqhan understanding. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as yafqahunu qawlan with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the qaf: from afqahu fulan kadha afqahu ifqaha: if you made him understand that. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that are widespread in the reading of the regions, neither of them contradicting the other. This is because the people about whom the narrator reported this information could have hardly understood what others said about them, so the reading would be correct according to that. It is also possible that, while they were like that, they could hardly understand others for reasons: either by their tongues or by their logic, so the reading according to that would also be correct.
18:94: And his saying, Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land. The reciters differed in the reading of his saying, Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land. The reciters from the people of Hijaz, Iraq, and others read Indeed, Gog and Magog without a hamza on the basis of fa'ul from yajjat and majjat, and they made the two alifs in them extra, except for Asim bin Abi al-Najud and al-A'raj, for he mentioned that they read it with a hamza in both of them, and they made the hamza in them from the root of the speech, and it is as if they made Yajuj: yaf'ul from ajajat, and ma'juj: maf'ul. The reading that is the correct reading according to us, is Indeed, Gog and Magog with an alif without a hamza, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, and that it is the well-known speech on the tongues of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Ru'bah bin al-'Ajaj: If Gog and Magog were together, 'Ad would return and seek help from them, and they are two nations from behind the dam. And his saying, Corrupters in the land, the people differed. Interpretation of the meaning of corruption that God described these two nations with. Some of them said: They were eating people. Mention of those who said that: Ahmad ibn al-Waleed al-Ramli told us: Ibrahim ibn Ayoub al-Khawzani told us: al-Waleed ibn Muslim told us: I heard Saeed ibn Abdul Aziz say about His statement, Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters on earth, that they used to eat people. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Gog and Magog will corrupt on earth, not that they were corrupters on that day. He mentioned who said that, and he mentioned the description of Dhul-Qarnayn’s following of the reasons mentioned by God in this verse, and he mentioned the reason for his building the dam: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us: Some of those who narrate the hadiths of the non-Arabs among the People of the Book, who had converted to Islam, told me about what they had inherited from the knowledge of Dhul-Qarnayn, that Dhul-Qarnayn was a man from the people of Egypt whose name was Marzumba ibn Mardaba the Greek, from the descendants of Yunun ibn Japheth ibn Noah. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan al-Kila’i - and Khalid was a man who had known the people - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he said: A king who wiped the earth from beneath it with means. Khalid said: Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man say: O Dhul-Qarnayn, so he said: O God, forgive me! Are you not satisfied to be named after the names of the prophets, even if you are named after the names of the angels? If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, then what he said is true, and what contradicts it is false. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Someone I do not suspect narrated to me on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who had knowledge of the first hadiths, that he used to say: Dhul-Qarnayn was a Roman man, the son of an old woman from among their old women, who had no other children but him, and his name was Alexander. He was called Dhul-Qarnayn because the sides of his head were made of copper. When he reached puberty and was a righteous slave, God, the Almighty, said to him: O Dhul-Qarnayn, I am sending you to the nations of the earth, and they are nations with different languages, and they are all the people of the earth, and among them are two nations between which is the entire length of the earth, and among them are two nations between which is the entire width of the earth, and nations in the middle of the earth, including the jinn and mankind and Gog and Magog. As for the two nations between which is the length of the earth: one is at the setting of the sun, and it is called Nasik. As for the other, it is at its rising, and it is called Mansak. As for the two between which is the width of the earth, there is a nation in the right part of the earth, and it is called Hawil. As for the other one in the left part of the earth, it is a nation called Tawil. When God said that to him, Dhul-Qarnayn said to him: My God, you have summoned me for a great matter that only you can estimate. So tell me about these nations to which you have sent me, with what strength I can overcome them, with what group I can outnumber them, with what trick I can outwit them, with what patience I can endure them, with what tongue I can speak to them, with what hearing I can comprehend their words, with what sight I can penetrate them, with what argument I can argue with them, with what heart I can reason about them, with what wisdom I can manage their affairs, with what equity I can be just between them, with what patience I can be patient with them, with what knowledge I can decide between them, with what science I can perfect their affairs, with what hand I can attack them, with what foot I can trample them, with what strength I can argue with them, with what army I can fight them, and with what kindness I can win them over. For I, my God, do not have anything of what you mentioned that can stand up to them, nor can it overcome them or endure them, and you are the Lord, the Merciful. He does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, nor burden it beyond its ability, nor does He oppress it nor burden it, but rather You are compassionate towards it and have mercy upon it. God the Almighty said: I will make you bear what I carry, I will expand your chest so that it can contain everything, I will expand your understanding so that you will understand everything, I will make your tongue easy for you so that you can speak everything, I will open your hearing so that you will comprehend everything, I will extend your sight so that you will implement everything, I will manage your affairs so that you will master everything, I will count for you so that nothing will escape you, I will protect you so that nothing will escape you, I will strengthen your back so that nothing will guide you, I will strengthen your pillar so that nothing will overcome you, I will strengthen your heart so that nothing will frighten you, I will subject light and darkness to you, so make them soldiers among your soldiers, the light will guide you before you and darkness will surround you from behind, I will strengthen your mind so that nothing will frighten you, I will make what is in front of you easy so that you can attack everything, I will strengthen your step so that you can defeat everything, I will clothe you with awe so that nothing will threaten you. When he was told that, he set out to lead the nation at sunset. When he reached them, he found a crowd and a number that only God could count, and a strength and might that no one could count. He could not bear it except God, and different tongues and scattered desires, and divided hearts. When he saw that, he overwhelmed them with darkness, so he set up three armies around them, and surrounded them from every side, and surrounded them until he gathered them in one place. Then he seized them with light, and called them to God and to His worship. Some of them believed in Him, and some of them turned away. So he went to those who turned away from Him, and he brought darkness upon them, so it entered their mouths, noses, ears, and cavities, and entered their homes and dwellings, and covered them from above them, and from below them, and from every side of them. So they raged in it and were confused. When they feared that they would perish in it, they raged to Him with one voice, so He removed it from them and took them by force, so they entered into his call. So he gathered from the people of the West great nations, and made them one army, then he set out with them leading them, and the darkness drove them from behind them and guarded them from around them, and the light was in front of them leading them and guiding them, and he walked in the right side of the earth, and he He wanted the nation in the right-hand corner of the earth called Hawil, and God made his hand, heart, opinion, mind, sight and command subservient to him, so he did not make a mistake when he commanded, and when he did something he did it perfectly. So he set out leading those nations and they followed him, and when he reached a sea or a ford, he built ships from small planks like sandals, and he arranged them in an hour, then he put in them all those with him from those nations and those soldiers, and when he crossed the rivers and seas, he split them, then he gave each person a plank so that he would not tire of carrying it, and he continued like that until he reached Hawil, and he worked in them as he would work in a hermit. When he finished it, he went on his way to the right side of the earth until he reached a place of worship at sunrise, and he worked there and recruited soldiers from it, as he had done with the two nations before it. Then he turned back towards the left side of the earth, and he wanted to go to Tawil, which is the nation opposite Hawil, and they are opposite each other, and between them is the entire width of the earth. When he reached it, he worked there and recruited soldiers from it as he had done with what came before it. When he finished it, he turned from it to the nations in the middle of the earth, from the jinn and the rest of the people, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was on some of the way, near the end of the Turk towards the east, a righteous nation of mankind said to him: O Dhul-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there are creatures from the creation of God, and many of them are similar to humans, and they are like beasts, they eat grass, and prey on animals and wild beasts as wild beasts prey on them, and they eat the vermin of the earth, all of them snakes and scorpions, and every living thing that God created on the earth. God has not created them to grow in one year, nor increase as they increase, nor multiply as they multiply. If they have a period of time, as we see of their growth and increase, then there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, and expel its people from it and prevail over it and spread corruption in it. Not a year passes since we have lived with them without us anticipating them and waiting for their first ones to appear to us from between these two mountains. Shall we give you an outlay on condition that you make between us and them a barrier? He said, What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength and I will make between you and them a barrier. Bring back to me the rocks, iron, and copper so that I may explore their lands, learn their knowledge, and measure what is between their two mountains. Then he set out to lead them until he reached them and was in the middle of their country. He found them to be of the same size, male and female. The height of each one of them was like half of a square man among us. They had claws in the place of fingernails on our hands, and molars and fangs like the molars and fangs of wild beasts, and jaws like the jaws of camels, strong. You could hear them move when they ate, like the movement of a camel’s jug, or like the chomping of an old stallion or a strong horse. They were hardy, with hair on their bodies that covered them and protected them from the heat and cold if they were to befall them. Each one of them had two large ears, one of which was furry on its back and belly. The other is the down of its back and belly, and it covers them both when it is worn, covering itself with one of them and spreading out the other, spending the summer in one of them and wintering in the other, and there is not a male or female among them except that he knows the time at which he will die, and the end of his life, and that is because no male among them dies until a thousand children come out of his loins, and no female dies until a thousand children come out of her womb, so when that happens death is certain, and they are provided with the dragons in the days of spring, and they ask for rain when they are waiting for it as we ask for rain at its time, so they throw one of them every year, and they eat it their entire year until the same of the next year, so it enriches them despite their abundance and growth, so when it rains and they are fertile and live and fat, and its effect is seen on them, then females are born to them, and the males from them are in heat, and if it misses them they become thin and barren, and the males are exhausted and the females dream, and the effect of that is clear on them, and they call each other like doves, and howl like dogs, and copulate wherever they meet Animal mating. When Dhul-Qarnayn saw that from them, he turned to the area between the two mountain-sides, and measured the distance between them, while he was in the farthest part of the land of the Turks, near the rising of the sun. He found that the distance between them was a hundred farsakhs. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached the water, then he made its width fifty farsakhs, and he made its filling rocks, and its clay copper, which was melted and then poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain that the earth was crushing. Then he rose and honored it with iron and molten copper, and made a vein of yellow copper in between it, so that it became like a reddish cloak of the yellowness of copper and the blackness of iron. When he had finished it and perfected it, he set out intentionally towards a group of humans and jinn. While he was traveling, he was brought to a righteous nation who guide with the truth and by it they are just. He found a nation that was fair and moderate, who divide equally, rule with justice, and are sympathetic and merciful to one another. Their condition is one, their word is one, their morals are similar, their way is upright, and their hearts are united. Their conduct was good, and their graves were at the doors of their houses, and there were no doors on their houses, and there were no princes over them, and there were no judges among them, and there were no rich, nor kings, nor nobles among them, and they did not differentiate between them, nor were they superior to each other, nor did they differ, nor did they quarrel, nor did they abuse each other, nor did they fight, nor did they suffer from drought, nor were they angry, nor were they afflicted with the plagues that afflict people, and they lived the longest lives of people, and there was no poor, nor needy, nor rude, nor coarse among them. When Dhul-Qarnayn saw that about them, he was amazed by it, and said: Tell me, O people, your story, for I have counted the entire earth, its land and sea, its east and west, its light and darkness, and I have not found anyone like you, so tell me your story. They said: Yes, so ask us whatever you want. He said: Tell me, why are the graves of your dead at the doors of your houses? They said: We did that intentionally so that we would not forget death, and its memory would not leave our hearts. He said: So why do your houses not have doors? They said: There is no one accused among us, and there is none among us who is not trustworthy and reliable. He said: So why is it that you have no rulers over you? They said: We do not wrong one another. He said: So why is it that you have no rulers among you? They said: We do not dispute. He said: So why is it that you have no rich people among you? They said: We do not compete with one another. He said: So why is it that you have no kings among you? They said: We do not act arrogantly. He said: So why do you not dispute or differ? They said: Because our hearts are in harmony and our relations are sound. He said: So why do you not insult one another or fight one another? They said: Because we have overcome our natures with determination, and have governed ourselves with patience. He said: So why is your word one, and your path straight and level? They said: Because we do not lie to one another, nor deceive one another, nor backbite one another. He said: So tell me, how did your hearts become alike and your conduct become straight? They said: Our hearts are sound, and thus rancor and envy were removed from our hearts. He said: So why is it that there is no poor or needy person among you? They said: Before, we used to divide equally. He said: So why is there no rude or harsh person among you? They said: Before, you were humble and modest. He said: So what made you the people with the longest lives? They said: Before, we used to deal with what is right and rule with justice. He said: So why are you not afflicted with drought? They said: We do not neglect to seek forgiveness. He said: So why are you not afflicted with hardship? They said: Before, we prepared ourselves for calamity since we were young, and we loved it and were keen on it, so we were stripped of it. He said: So why are calamities not befalling you as they befall people? They said: We do not trust in anyone but God, and we do not act according to the signs and stars. He said: Tell me, did you find your fathers doing this? They said: Yes, we found our fathers having mercy on their poor and comforting their needy, forgiving those who wronged them, being good to those who mistreated them, being patient with those who were ignorant of them, asking forgiveness for those who insulted them, maintaining family ties, fulfilling their trusts, preserving their time for prayer, fulfilling their promises, being truthful in their appointments, not turning away from their equals, and not being disdainful of their relatives. So God put their affairs right for them and preserved them as long as they were alive, and it was God’s right to preserve them in their estate. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Rafi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Gog and Magog dig the dam every day, until they see the rays of the sun. Then God says: Go back and dig it tomorrow. Then God restores it to the state it was in when they left it. Then when the time comes, He says: God willing. So they dig it and come out to the people and dry up the water, and the people fortify themselves in their forts, and they throw their arrows towards the sky, and they return with them like blood, and they say: We have defeated the people of the earth, and we have overcome the people of the heaven. Then God sends upon them a scorpion in their necks and it kills them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth grow fat and thank God for their flesh. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada al-Ansari then al-Dhafri, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, the brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Gog and Magog will be conquered and will come out upon the people as God, the Almighty, has said. They will come down from every side and cover the earth. The Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and they will gather their livestock with them and drink the waters of the earth. Some of them will pass by a river and drink what is in it until they leave it dry. Some of them will pass by that river and say: ‘There was water here once,’ until there is no one left among the people who has not withdrawn to a fortress or a city. One of them will say: ‘These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. The people of heaven remain.’ Then one of them will shake his spear and throw it into the sky, and it will return to him covered in blood as a result of the affliction and tribulation. While they are on…” Then, God sent worms in their necks like mites, and they came out in their necks and they became dead, and no sound was heard from them. The Muslims said: Is there not a man who will sell himself for us, so he can see what the enemy has done? He said: So a man from them will strip himself for that, hoping for reward for himself, and he has prepared it for himself that he will be killed. So he goes down and finds them dead, one on top of the other, and he calls out: O group of Muslims? Do not rejoice, for God has sufficed you against your enemy. So they come out of their cities and fortresses, and they let their livestock go out, and they have no grazing except their flesh, and they are grateful for them better than they are grateful for any plant they have ever eaten. Bahr bin Nasr told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahariyyah and Shureih bin Ubaid: Gog and Magog are of three types: a type whose height is like the height of a cedar, a type whose height and width are the same, and a type whose ear is spread out and the other is covered so that it covers the rest of his body. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, They said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land.’ He said: Abu Sa`id al-Khudri used to say: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Not a single one of them will die until a thousand men are born to his loins. He said: `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud used to marvel at their great number and say: Not a single one of Gog and Magog will die until a thousand men are born to him from his loins. The report that we mentioned from Wahb bin Munabbih in the story of Gog and Magog indicates that those who said to Dhul-Qarnayn, Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, only informed him of their fear of what they would do of corruption in the land, not that they suspected any corruption from them in themselves or in others. The reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are that they would cause corruption in the land, and there is no indication in them that they had caused corruption in the land before Dhul-Qarnayn created the barrier that he built between them and those other than them from the people. If that is the case with what we have explained, then the correct interpretation of his statement, Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land, is that Gog and Magog will cause corruption in the land. And his statement, Then shall we make for you a burden? The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so most of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it, Then shall we make for you a burden? as if they had made it similar to the source of the root to go out of the head, and that is what they made it. The majority of Kufi readers read it as Falla nanja’il laka kharj with an alif, as if they had made it a noun, and meant by it a fee for your building a dam between us and these people. The first of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the correct reading of the one who reads it Fall we make nk kharaj with an alif, because the people, as has been reported about them, only offered Dhul-Qarnayn to give him from their wealth what would help him build the dam, and he explained that by saying So help me with strength, I will make between you and them a barrier, and they did not offer him a tribute on their heads. Kharaj among the Arabs is the yield. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said about that. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Shall we give you a tax? He said: A reward, on condition that you make a barrier between us and them. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Shall We then make for you a tribute? He said: A wage. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then shall we make for you a tribute? He said: A wage. And his statement, On condition that you place between us and them a barrier? He said: They said to him: Shall we make for you a tribute until you place between us and Gog and Magog a barrier that will stand between us and them and prevent them from coming out to us? And it is the barrier.
18:95: God Almighty says: Dhul-Qarnayn said: The one who enabled me to do what you asked me to do of the dam between you and these people is my Lord, and He made it easy for me and strengthened me over it. He is better than what you have made, and the wage that you offer me for building that is more and better, but help me from among you with strength, help me with work and craftsmen who are good at building and working. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, What my Lord has empowered me in is better, so help me with strength. He said: With men. I will place between you and them a barrier. He said: What He has empowered me in, so he assimilated one of the two noons into the other, but it is what He has empowered me in. And His saying: I will place between you and them a barrier means: I will place between you and Gog and Magog a barrier. And the barrier is the barrier of a wall and a dam, except that it is more impenetrable and stronger. It is said from it: So-and-so has blocked such-and-such a place, he blocks it with a block and a barrier. And it is also said: He blocked his garment and he blocks it, and it is a patched garment: if it has many patches, and from it is the saying of Antarah: Did the poets leave the ruins or did you know the house after the illusion? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Shall I place between you and them a barrier? He said: It is like the strictest barrier. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that a man said: O Prophet of God, I have seen the dam of Gog and Magog. He said: Describe it to me. He said: It is like ink-coloured hail, one path is black and the other is red. He said: I have seen it.
18:96: The Almighty says: Dhul-Qarnayn said to those who asked him to build a barrier between them and Gog and Magog, Bring me: meaning, bring me iron bars, which is the plural of zibra, and zibra is a piece of iron. As Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying pieces of iron means: pieces of iron. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Bring me sheets of iron, he said: pieces of iron. Ismail bin Saif told me: Ali bin Mashair told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, regarding his statement, pieces of iron, he said: pieces of iron. Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaid God bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Bring me sheets of iron, he said: pieces of iron. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Bring me sheets of iron: meaning split iron. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Bring me sheets of iron, he said: pieces of iron. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Bring me sheets of iron. He said: pieces of iron. And His statement, Until, when he had leveled between the two mountain-sides, the Almighty says: So they brought him sheets of iron, and he placed them between the two mountain-sides until, when he had leveled between the two mountains with what he had placed between them of sheets of iron. It is said: he leveled. The two mountain-sides is what is between the sides of the two mountains and their tops, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: I took what was between the width of the two sides of the shells and the tops of the two corners. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, between the two mountain-sides, meaning: between the two mountains. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Ait, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Until when he reached between the two mountains. He said: It was a mountain between two mountains. The two mountains are the two mountains. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement the two mountaintops means the tops of the two mountains. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, between the two mountain ranges, meaning the two mountains, which are on the side of Armenia and Azerbaijan.
